title: A product of two smooth algebras over one base is smooth
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $S'$, $S''$ be commutative $R$-algebras, with structure maps $\psi':R\to S'$ and $\psi'':R\to S''$. Make the product ring $S'\times S''$ (componentwise operations, unit $(1,1)$) an $R$-algebra via $r\mapsto(\psi'(r),\psi''(r))$. If $R\to S'$ and $R\to S''$ are smooth ring maps [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], then $R\to S'\times S''$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0GIF (lemma-product-smooth, line 37613), hint of the omitted proof: Lemma Tag 00TC (lemma-locally-smooth, line 37572) and Lemma Tag 00ED (lemma-spec-product, line 3822, whose proof says R_1 = R_{e_1})

proof.text: Lift S' and S'' to the common universe max v w, using ULift.algEquiv and smoothness invariant under algebra equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-isomorphism-invariant]. Define the Fin 2 family A by these two lifted factors, with its componentwise commutative-ring and R-algebra structures.

Smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] supplies formal smoothness and finite presentation for each A i. Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.instForallOfFinite and Algebra.FinitePresentation.pi supply both properties for the finite dependent product, hence Smooth R (forall i, A i).

Upgrade RingEquiv.piFinTwo A to an R-algebra equivalence: scalar compatibility is definitional. Transfer smoothness to the binary product and then to S' x S'' by AlgEquiv.prodCongr of the ULift algebra equivalences, using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-isomorphism-invariant].
